decisions.statement: An argument is read by the slug the name after the page type carries.
What is read of an argument is how it is spelled, what it carries and what it is for.
The arguments are answered in the order the command names them.
An argument name reaching no page is answered with nothing in its place.
A page stating neither how it is said nor what it is for is no argument here.
A command naming no argument is answered without the index being read.
Nothing here writes a help answer.
An argument is written down the way the command naming it lets a call fill it.
An argument taken at its flag is written down as that flag and its placeholder.
An argument stating no placeholder is written down as its flag alone.
An argument taken as a word is written down as its placeholder alone.
A word argument stating no placeholder is written down by its slug.
An argument taken either way is written down as a word and then at its flag.
A placeholder is written in the angle brackets a page leaves off it.

definition: the argument pages a command names, as the index carries what each one states
